panels.narrative: Jed reached out with his left hand, his fingers trembling as he pulled his personal smartphone from his pocket. It was an itch beneath the dermis, a geometric irritation that felt as though his DNA were being recompiled into a more efficient syntax. He raised the phone to scan the code on the wall, driven by a clinical, investigative dread.
She was The Recorder; her role was to witness the arrival, not to prevent it. The camera app struggled to focus. On the screen, the QR code on the poster didn't lead to a URL.

Instead, the white spaces between the black modules began to darken, not with shadow, but with substance. A thick, dark crimson liquid began to well up from the pixels on the phone’s display. It didn't sit on top of the glass; it emerged *through* it, bubbling out of the rendered image as if the hardware were a porous membrane.
The blood was unnaturally bright, smelling of iron and sacramental wine.
